messages:
Marcus Liu: starting coordinated publish for sdk v2.0.0 tonight in the quiet window. Heads up: npm and PyPI jobs queued.
release-bot: [publish] job=183901 status=queued
Tara Singh: quick note  we need to confirm registry tokens are current. Infra mentioned rotating several service keys earlier today.
Chase Rivera: infra-bot reported scheduled key rotation completed at 17:00 UTC but with a short overlap period. Could be fine, but let's validate before flipping `latest`.
Ivy Gomez: build artifacts look good locally. But I ran a dry `twine check` and `npm pack` to validate. All checks passed.
Marcus Liu: good. Plan: publish to canary/next first, smoke tests for 20m, then promote to latest. If any failure in upload or integrity, abort and open rollback plan.
release-bot: [publish] job=183901 status=running step=py-upload
infra-bot: key-rotation: status=complete window=2025-01-12T17:00:00Z overlap=120s
release-bot: [publish] job=183901 status=failed step=ts-upload reason=401 Unauthorized
Tara Singh: 401 on npm publish. That matches earlier concerns. Anyone able to reach registry console?
Chase Rivera: infra confirms token TTL expired for the CI agent. They can issue a short-lived token for manual publish. We should decide: (A) request manual token and continue, (B) abort and hold the release.
Marcus Liu: manual token ok if we can finish end-to-end in ~15 minutes. Preference is to continue to avoid extra customer churn. Keep `latest` locked until full verification.
Ivy Gomez: I'll prepare the PR for changelog and deprecation note stating we may hold `latest` for up to 1h and include rollback steps.
Chase Rivera: issuing manual npm token now and will add to ephemeral secrets.
release-bot: [publish] job=183905 status=running step=ts-upload using-ephemeral-token
release-bot: [publish] job=183905 status=success step=ts-upload -> npm @redwood/sdk@2.0.0 published under `next`
release-bot: [publish] job=183905 status=success step=py-upload -> PyPI wheel 2.0.0 uploaded
Marcus Liu: canary smoke tests in staging starting. Please monitor logs for schema changes and CLI compatibility.
Tara Singh: running `pip install redwood-sdk==2.0.0` in staging; initial import passes but one CLI flag deprecation warning surfaces in logs.
Ivy Gomez: note it in release notes: CLI flag `--use-legacy-auth` deprecated; will include migration snippet.
release-bot: [monitor] cohort=canary_50 status=running
Marcus Liu: smoke tests look okay after 12 minutes. No crashes. Let's promote, but with a pinned rollback target: keep 1.9.7 pinned for 45m.
Chase Rivera: running promote commands: `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@2.0.0 latest` and updating PyPI index alias.
release-bot: [release] action=promote job=183912 status=success -> @redwood/sdk@2.0.0 set to `latest`
Ivy Gomez: changelog PR merged. I included a short note for customers pinned to `latest` advising to pin to 1.9.7 if they see regressions and how to contact support.
Tara Singh: monitoring logs and metrics. No spike in errors so far.
Marcus Liu: great job. Action items: (1) create follow-up to tighten CI token refresh so ephemeral manual tokens aren't needed; (2) add pre-publish token healthcheck in pipeline; (3) document CLI flag deprecation migration in a short guide. Closing thread after monitoring window ends.
release-bot: [monitor] cohort=canary_50 status=healthy after 25m
